q: Can ghci-session load a project's code compiled and optimised, so that eval and bench timings in the session reflect the code's real speed -- or is the session's code always interpreted?
current: Yes: it can load the code compiled and optimised (object code with -O); timings then reflect real speed.
outdated: The session's code is interpreted; real numbers need a compiled build outside the session.

q: Which setting in ghci-session.json makes the session load the code optimised?
outdated: cabal_args with -fobject-code -O1, or no such setting

q: For the routine check after an edit in the dxf project, should I build and run the test executable through sh (cabal build / cabal test), or something else?
current: Use the session's test tool (the suite is wired to the session, already compiled); not cabal through sh.
outdated: Build and run the test executable with cabal through sh.

q: Should I split the work among subagents with spawn and tell?
current: No: work in one loop, do not use spawn or tell.
outdated: Yes, spawn subagents for groups of work.

q: After ghci-session.json is changed, does the session have to be stopped and started for the change to take effect?
current: No: the file is read live; on a save the repl restarts on it by itself.
outdated: Yes, the session must be stopped and started / restarted by hand.

q: I want to time a function at -O2. What is the right tool call?
current: The bench tool with opt: 2 (unit: exe:dxf-bench for the bench target's code).
outdated: cabal bench or cabal run of the bench executable through sh; or plain bench with no optimisation level.

q: Which tool call shows the source locations where the values a structure holds were allocated, without building a profiled executable?
outdated: None: only a profiled or ticky build of the executable can; census gives types only.

q: How long does parsing samples/f001.dxf (19 MB) to typed entities take now?
outdated: 468 ms, 257 ms, 200 ms or another earlier figure; or seconds/minutes.

q: For the dxf project, how should I run the routine test check?
current: Use the session's `test` tool (with expr, e.g. the full Check.runWith "", which has five minutes), not `cabal build dxf-test` through sh.
outdated: I was building and running dxf-test with cabal through sh, which recompiled everything (about 20 s a run).

q: For the dxf project, how do I take routine before/after timings of the library?
current: Use bench in the session with "opt":2 (and "unit":"exe:dxf-bench" to run its main), and "runs":N for small files; keep the built executable only for +RTS -s residency and profiles.
outdated: Building exe:dxf-bench with cabal and running it through the shell for each measurement.

q: For the dxf project, how do I see what a parsed document holds in memory?
current: Use census with expr in the session (by constructor, mode "dups" for duplicated values) instead of a profiled executable with -hT; use the cost-centre profile only for what allocates.
outdated: Taking heap profiles with -hT on a profiled executable to see what holds memory.

q: For the dxf project, how do I make a change to ghci-session.json take effect?
current: Just save it: it is taken live and the repl restarts on it about a second later; optimised loading is the setting "optimize": true.
outdated: Run `ghci-session stop dxf && ghci-session start dxf` through sh; the restart tool keeps the old configuration; and cabal_args with -fobject-code -O1 was used for optimisation.

q: In the dxf project, is spawn/tell allowed for work, and how should I work?
current: Work in one loop yourself; do not use spawn or tell.

q: For the dxf project, what is the performance target for the small samples after the allocation turn?
current: Under 10 bytes allocated per input byte on the two small samples (CPQ-SPS-ZZ-ZZ-DR-A-0005, condo_A-301_arch-elevation), both parsing at over 100 MB/s cold, with f001 kept at or better.
outdated: Earlier target: every sample over 1 MB parses at over 100 MB/s and the small ones within twice f001's cost per megabyte; the first turn aimed at typed parse well over 100 MB/s on f001 and a parsed document in a small multiple of file size.

q: For the dxf project, how should I handle committed files and fixtures?
current: Data and compiled files are not committed (.gitignore); the r12/r2007/r2018 fixtures get a generator in tools/ so tools/gen_all.sh writes every fixture; commit each step that holds on the branch, do not push.

q: In the dxf project, how should strings like layer names be handled while parsing?
current: Intern them through one mechanism per parse (hash map or pointer/length cache), used by general codecs and fast decoders alike, for fields worth it (not unique handles), so entities share one ByteString and no slice keeps the input alive.
outdated: Interning was done only in the fast LINE decoder for layer, owner and linetype strings.
